text: The urinalysis results show no signs of infection, so we can rule that out as a primary cause of your symptoms. Moving to your neurological issues: do you notice any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis confirms no urinary tract infection, which aligns with your one-year history of incontinence. You mentioned recent speech slurring; do you also experience difficulty swallowing food or liquids, or any involuntary muscle movements like twitching or jerking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
You mention rigidity, mild hand tremor, and orthostatic hypotension alongside your gait and speech issues; do you notice any stiffness in your neck or shoulders that makes it difficult to move your head?

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (MSA), specifically the Parkinsonian variant (MSA-P), given the combination of cerebellar ataxia, autonomic failure (orthostatic hypotension, incontinence), and parkinsonian features (rigidity, tremor).
